questions.stem: During a surgical procedure using electrocautery, a newer team member questions why the smoke evacuation system needs to run continuously when the surgical field already looks clear. The nurse should explain that this system is used primarily to:
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Reduce the overall equipment costs associated with the surgical procedure, which is not the actual reason for its use","B":"Speed up the pace at which the surgical procedure itself is completed, which is not the actual reason for its use","C":"Reduce staff exposure to surgical smoke, which can contain harmful chemicals and biological material even when the field appears visually clear","D":"Improve only the surgeon's visibility of the field, with no health-related benefit, despite the actual health-protective purpose of the system"}}
questions.rationale: Surgical smoke generated by electrocautery or lasers can contain harmful chemicals, particulates, and potentially biological material. Smoke evacuation systems are used to reduce staff exposure to these hazards, protecting the respiratory health of the surgical team.
questions.source_name: AORN — Surgical Smoke Safety Guideline

questions.stem: During a procedure using a surgical laser, a new team member puts on standard sunglasses instead of the eyewear provided at the door, assuming any dark lens will work. All personnel in the room, including the client, should instead wear:
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Protective eyewear worn just when a person is directly facing toward the laser beam, rather than throughout the procedure","B":"Skipping eye protection entirely, contrary to what is actually required for everyone present during this kind of procedure","C":"Wavelength-specific protective eyewear appropriate for the particular laser being used, not standard sunglasses like the new team member put on","D":"Standard, non-specialized sunglasses, similar to what the new team member assumed would be sufficient"}}
questions.rationale: Laser procedures require wavelength-specific protective eyewear for all personnel in the room, including the client (when applicable), since standard eyewear (including regular sunglasses) does not provide adequate protection against the specific wavelength of the laser being used, and eye injury can occur even without direct exposure.
questions.source_name: AORN — Laser Safety Guideline

questions.stem: A nurse is preparing a client for an MRI scan, and the client mentions feeling completely calm and not at all anxious about the procedure. A critical safety screening step the nurse must still complete, regardless of the client's calm demeanor, is to:
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Screen the client and environment for any ferromagnetic objects or implanted devices that could pose a hazard in the strong magnetic field","B":"Skipping the screening process since the client appears calm and cooperative, reasoning anxious clients are the main concern to watch for","C":"Letting metal objects and jewelry stay on the client during the scan without any prior screening whatsoever taking place","D":"Assuming any implanted medical device the client might have is automatically considered safe for MRI without verification first"}}
questions.rationale: MRI safety screening is critical because the powerful magnetic field can cause ferromagnetic objects to become dangerous projectiles, and certain implanted devices (such as some pacemakers or aneurysm clips) may be unsafe or malfunction in the MRI environment. Thorough screening of the client, accompanying persons, and environment is essential before the scan.
questions.source_name: ACR (American College of Radiology) — MRI Safety Guidance

questions.stem: A hospital implements a program to monitor staff hand hygiene compliance rates. This practice is an example of:
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"A purely punitive measure implemented with no accompanying educational component","B":"An unnecessary use of hospital resources with no genuine patient safety benefit, since hand hygiene compliance is already assumed to be high","C":"A quality improvement strategy to identify gaps and improve adherence to a key infection prevention practice","D":"A monitoring practice that has no established relationship to actual patient outcomes"}}
questions.rationale: Hand hygiene compliance monitoring is a recognized quality improvement strategy that helps healthcare facilities identify gaps in adherence to this foundational infection prevention practice, guiding targeted education and interventions to improve compliance and, ultimately, patient safety.
questions.source_name: CDC / WHO — Hand Hygiene Compliance Monitoring Programs

questions.stem: During a severe shortage of personal protective equipment, a facility implements "crisis capacity" PPE strategies, and a nurse assumes this means PPE is essentially optional now for certain routine tasks. The nurse should understand these strategies actually:
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Eliminating the need for personal protective equipment during direct, hands-on client contact, contrary to what these strategies actually involve","B":"Representing the facility's preferred, standard approach to PPE use even when conventional supplies are fully available and plentiful","C":"Applying only to non-clinical support staff rather than to those providing direct client care, contrary to how these strategies actually apply","D":"Temporary, extraordinary measures like extended use or limited reuse of PPE, used only when conventional and contingency supplies are exhausted"}}
questions.rationale: Crisis capacity PPE strategies are temporary, extraordinary measures (such as extended use or limited reuse of certain PPE items) implemented only when conventional and contingency supplies are exhausted during a severe shortage, per CDC guidance, and are not the preferred standard approach under normal circumstances.
questions.source_name: CDC — Strategies for Optimizing PPE Supplies

questions.stem: During a mass casualty incident, triage tags are used to categorize victims. A victim tagged "red" typically indicates:
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Immediate, life-threatening injuries requiring urgent intervention","B":"Minor injuries that can wait for care","C":"Deceased or expectant, with no immediate intervention planned","D":"Delayed but serious injuries that can wait a period of time"}}
questions.rationale: In standard disaster triage color-coding systems, "red" indicates immediate, life-threatening injuries requiring urgent intervention, while other colors (yellow for delayed, green for minor/walking wounded, and black for deceased/expectant) categorize victims by relative urgency of need.
questions.source_name: START Triage System / Disaster Medicine Standards
questions.source_detail: Red Tag Classification in Mass Casualty Triage

questions.stem: A nurse is preparing an isolation cart outside a client's room who requires contact precautions. The cart should be stocked with:
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"No specific supplies at all, since each staff member is expected to bring their own in this particular case","B":"Only surgical masks, regardless of the specific type of precaution required, since one type of mask is considered sufficient for any isolation type","C":"Gowns, gloves, and other PPE appropriate for the specific type of precautions required, along with signage indicating the precaution type","D":"Only a bottle of hand sanitizer, with no other protective supplies included on the prepared isolation cart"}}
questions.rationale: An isolation cart should be stocked with the appropriate PPE (gowns, gloves, and additional items as needed such as masks or eye protection) specific to the type of precautions required (contact, droplet, or airborne), along with clear signage, to support consistent and correct staff compliance.
questions.source_name: CDC — Isolation Precautions Supply and Signage Guidance

questions.stem: A client requiring airborne precautions is being placed in a room, and a newer staff member suggests any private room with the door closed will work just as well. The nurse should recognize the client should ideally be placed in a room with which special feature instead?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Negative pressure ventilation, which actively prevents contaminated air from flowing out into adjacent areas, unlike the plain private room the newer staff member suggested","B":"Standard room ventilation identical to what is used for any other hospitalized client currently on the unit at this particular time","C":"No specific ventilation requirements beyond the room's baseline airflow, similar to what the newer staff member had suggested earlier today","D":"Positive pressure ventilation, which would actually push contaminated air out into the adjacent areas rather than contain it properly in this scenario"}}
questions.rationale: Airborne infection isolation rooms (AIIRs) require negative pressure ventilation, which ensures that air flows into the room rather than out into adjacent hallways or areas, helping contain airborne pathogens and protect other clients and staff outside the room.
questions.source_name: CDC — Airborne Infection Isolation Room Requirements
questions.source_detail: Negative Pressure Ventilation for Airborne Precautions

questions.stem: A float pool nurse with a strong medical-surgical background is assigned to a specialty pediatric ICU unit outside their usual area of practice, and the charge nurse begins handing out full client assignments right away. Before this float nurse assumes a full client assignment, the facility should first ensure:
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"The float nurse being deliberately given the single most complex client assignment available on the pediatric ICU that particular day","B":"The nurse being expected to work entirely alone with no available resource support, given their strong general medical-surgical background","C":"No orientation or competency verification being required before assuming the assignment, given the nurse's overall years of experience","D":"The nurse's competency for this unit's patient population has actually been verified, with appropriate orientation and support first"}}
questions.rationale: Facilities have a responsibility to verify a float pool nurse's competency for the specific patient population and skills required on an unfamiliar unit, providing appropriate orientation and support, and typically avoiding assignment of the most complex clients to a nurse unfamiliar with that specialty.
questions.source_name: ANA — Principles for Nurse Staffing, Float Pool Considerations

questions.stem: During a hospital's response to a large-scale disaster, staff operate under an Incident Command System (ICS), and a new staff member assumes this is just a temporary renaming of the usual chain of command with no real functional difference. This system is primarily designed to:
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Applying just to law enforcement agencies, with fairly little relevance to healthcare settings like the one currently responding here","B":"Eliminating the need for any organizational structure during the response, contrary to what ICS actually provides in this kind of event","C":"Permanently replacing the hospital's existing policies without exception, rather than serving its actual, more limited purpose in this kind of context","D":"Provide a standardized, scalable organizational structure for coordinating an effective emergency response, which is more than just a renaming of the usual chain of command"}}
questions.rationale: The Incident Command System (ICS) provides a standardized, scalable organizational structure used to coordinate personnel, resources, and communication during an emergency response, applicable across various settings including hospitals, to promote an effective, organized response to disasters or large-scale incidents.
questions.source_name: FEMA / Hospital Incident Command System (HICS) — Emergency Management Framework
questions.source_detail: Purpose of the Incident Command System

questions.stem: A nurse working in a telephone triage role uses standardized protocols to help callers determine the urgency of their symptoms, and a caller becomes frustrated, demanding the nurse just tell them exactly what condition they have. This practice actually requires the nurse to:
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Providing a definitive medical diagnosis to every caller over the phone, without much regard for symptom complexity, as this caller demands","B":"Use validated clinical decision-support protocols and sound clinical judgment to guide callers to the right level and timing of care","C":"Avoiding documentation of the call details in the client's medical record, since triage calls aren't considered part of the formal record","D":"Ignoring caller-reported symptoms and relying just on the written protocol without applying any actual clinical judgment"}}
questions.rationale: Telephone triage nursing practice involves using validated clinical decision-support protocols, combined with sound nursing clinical judgment, to help callers determine the appropriate level and timing of care needed (such as emergency care, urgent care, or self-care at home), along with thorough documentation of the encounter.
questions.source_name: American Academy of Ambulatory Care Nursing — Telephone Triage Practice Standards

questions.stem: A client expresses interest in obtaining a second medical opinion before proceeding with a major surgery. The nurse should:
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Inform the client that seeking a second opinion is never permitted by the facility","B":"Actively discourage the client from pursuing a second medical opinion","C":"Support the client's right to seek a second opinion, which is a recognized patient right","D":"Assume the client is inappropriately questioning the current provider's competence"}}
questions.rationale: Seeking a second opinion is a recognized patient right, allowing individuals to gather additional information and perspectives before making significant healthcare decisions. The nurse should support and facilitate this process rather than discourage it, respecting client autonomy.
questions.source_name: Patient Bill of Rights — Right to Seek a Second Opinion
questions.source_detail: Nursing Support for Patient Autonomy in Seeking Second Opinions

questions.stem: A nurse is explaining the difference between a healthcare proxy (healthcare power of attorney) and a general power of attorney to a client's adult child, who assumes the two documents cover exactly the same authority. The nurse should clarify that a healthcare proxy specifically:
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Grants the designated person authority over the client's financial affairs, with fairly little healthcare decision-making role involved","B":"Grants a designated person authority to make healthcare decisions for the client if they become unable to do so themselves","C":"Is identical in legal scope to a general, non-healthcare power of attorney covering just financial matters and transactions","D":"Has fairly little formal legal standing in healthcare decision-making, functioning just as an informal expression of preference"}}
questions.rationale: A healthcare proxy (or healthcare power of attorney) specifically grants a designated person the legal authority to make healthcare decisions on the client's behalf if they become incapacitated or otherwise unable to make decisions themselves, distinct from a general power of attorney, which may cover broader or different areas such as financial affairs.
questions.source_name: National POLST / Advance Care Planning Resources — Healthcare Proxy Definition

questions.stem: A client has a Do Not Resuscitate (DNR) order in place, and a new nursing assistant asks whether this means the client should no longer receive pain medication or routine care. The nurse should clarify that this order specifically applies to:
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Withholding all forms of medical treatment, including pain management and routine nursing care, as the nursing assistant is currently assuming","B":"Preventing the client from receiving any form of ongoing nursing care whatsoever, including comfort measures, as the nursing assistant is currently assuming","C":"Withholding cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) specifically, in the event of cardiac or respiratory arrest, while all other appropriate care, including pain management, continues as usual","D":"Automatically applying to every future hospitalization with no need for reassessment at each new admission, contrary to how DNR orders actually need to be handled"}}
questions.rationale: A DNR order specifically addresses withholding cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) in the event of cardiac or respiratory arrest. It does not mean withholding other appropriate medical treatment, comfort care, or routine nursing care, and the scope should be clearly understood by the entire care team.
questions.source_name: National POLST / AHA — DNR Order Scope and Clarification

questions.stem: A client with a significant cognitive impairment has a legally appointed guardian, but the client's adult sibling, who visits frequently, insists they should be the one making healthcare decisions instead. The nurse understands that healthcare decisions for this client should generally be directed to:
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"The person holding formal legal authority for this decision, since that authority does not shift just because someone else visits often","B":"Any family member who happens to be present at the client's bedside at the time, such as the sibling currently insisting on this role","C":"No one, since a guardianship designation is mistakenly assumed here to have no bearing on healthcare decisions","D":"The client alone, with the appointed guardian having no role, based on the mistaken assumption that guardianship applies only to financial matters"}}
questions.rationale: When a client has a legally appointed guardian (established through a formal legal process due to incapacity), healthcare decisions are generally directed to the guardian, who has been granted legal authority to make decisions on the client's behalf, while still involving the client to the extent possible.
questions.source_name: Legal and Ethical Foundations of Nursing Practice — Guardianship
questions.source_detail: Role of Legal Guardian in Healthcare Decision-Making

questions.stem: A nurse manager is comparing typical nurse-to-patient staffing ratios between an intensive care unit (ICU) and a general medical-surgical unit. The nurse manager understands that ICU ratios are generally:
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Lower (fewer patients per nurse) than medical-surgical units, reflecting the higher acuity and closer monitoring needs of critically ill clients","B":"A ratio that has no established relationship to client safety or clinical outcomes, since staffing levels are determined solely by budget","C":"A ratio that is identical to medical-surgical units across every single healthcare facility nationwide","D":"Higher, meaning more clients assigned to each nurse than on a medical-surgical unit, reflecting lower acuity needs"}}
questions.rationale: ICU nurse-to-patient ratios are generally lower (fewer patients assigned per nurse, such as 1:1 or 1:2) compared to general medical-surgical units, reflecting the higher acuity, complexity, and closer monitoring needs of critically ill clients in intensive care settings.
questions.source_name: ANA / AACN — Staffing Ratio Considerations by Unit Acuity
questions.source_detail: ICU vs. Medical-Surgical Staffing Ratio Differences

questions.stem: A client diagnosed with acute compartment syndrome is being prepared for treatment. The nurse should anticipate the need for:
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Simple elevation of the affected limb alone, with no further intervention needed","B":"Emergency fasciotomy, a surgical procedure to relieve pressure within the affected compartment","C":"Oral pain medication alone, with no surgical intervention planned or anticipated","D":"Application of an additional, tighter cast or dressing over the affected limb"}}
questions.rationale: Acute compartment syndrome is a surgical emergency requiring prompt fasciotomy — a surgical procedure that releases the fascia to relieve dangerously elevated pressure within the affected muscle compartment, preventing permanent tissue and nerve damage. Delaying treatment risks limb loss.
questions.source_name: American Academy of Orthopaedic Surgeons — Acute Compartment Syndrome Treatment

questions.stem: A client in diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA) has a serum potassium level of 3.0 mEq/L before insulin therapy begins. The nurse should anticipate that the provider will:
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Start insulin therapy immediately, with no particular attention paid to the client's current serum potassium level","B":"Administer a potassium-wasting diuretic immediately, before starting insulin therapy, in order to further lower the serum potassium level","C":"Withhold all treatment entirely until the serum potassium level has fully normalized before ever starting the client's insulin therapy","D":"Address the low potassium level (often with potassium replacement) before or concurrently with starting insulin, since insulin therapy will further lower serum potassium"}}
questions.rationale: Insulin therapy drives potassium into cells, further lowering an already low serum potassium level, which can precipitate dangerous cardiac arrhythmias. When a client in DKA has hypokalemia, potassium replacement is typically addressed before or concurrently with starting insulin therapy, per standard DKA management protocols.
questions.source_name: American Diabetes Association — DKA Management Guidelines

questions.stem: A nurse is trying to distinguish between serotonin syndrome and neuroleptic malignant syndrome (NMS) in a client with altered mental status and elevated temperature. One key distinguishing feature is that serotonin syndrome typically presents with:
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Findings that are identical between the two conditions, with no distinguishing features at all in this particular clinical scenario overall","B":"Hyperreflexia and myoclonus, whereas NMS more typically presents with significant \"lead-pipe\" muscle rigidity","C":"An absence of any neuromuscular findings in either of these two conditions","D":"Hypothermia as the hallmark feature, whereas NMS is instead characterized by hyperthermia"}}
questions.rationale: While both conditions can present with altered mental status and hyperthermia, serotonin syndrome is more typically associated with hyperreflexia, myoclonus (muscle jerks), and gastrointestinal symptoms, whereas NMS is more classically associated with significant, uniform "lead-pipe" muscle rigidity and a more gradual onset, though clinical overlap can occur.
questions.source_name: Cleveland Clinic — Serotonin Syndrome vs. NMS Distinguishing Features
questions.source_detail: Key Clinical Differences Between the Two Syndromes

questions.stem: A client is treated successfully for anaphylaxis and symptoms resolve. The nurse should still recommend a period of observation because:
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"A biphasic reaction (recurrence of anaphylaxis symptoms) can occur hours after the initial resolution, even without re-exposure to the trigger","B":"The client can safely be discharged immediately with no further period of monitoring following the initial treatment","C":"A period of observation is never considered medically necessary after treated anaphylaxis in this particular clinical scenario overall","D":"No meaningful risk of the client's symptoms recurring after the initial treatment, since anaphylaxis is considered a single, self-limited event"}}
questions.rationale: A biphasic anaphylactic reaction, in which symptoms recur hours after apparent resolution of the initial episode (without re-exposure to the trigger), is a recognized phenomenon. A period of observation after treatment, along with clear instructions to seek care if symptoms recur, is recommended.
questions.source_name: World Allergy Organization — Anaphylaxis Guidance, Biphasic Reactions
questions.source_detail: Risk and Recognition of Biphasic Anaphylaxis
